thread.title: Legal Challenge to Florida's HB 3 Social Media Law
thread.title_full: Legal Challenge to Florida's HB 3 Social Media Law

author: Phil Ammann
title: Legal Challenge to Florida's HB 3 Social Media Law
text:
• A legal battle is underway in Florida regarding HB 3, a law aimed at protecting young people from social media.
• The Computer & Communications Industry Association (CCIA) is challenging HB 3 in court, claiming it violates First Amendment rights.
• Oral arguments for the case are scheduled for Friday.
• HB 3 was signed into law by Governor Ron DeSantis in March 2024 and is set to take effect on January 1, 2025.
• The law prohibits children under 14 from having social media accounts and requires parental permission for those aged 14 and 15.
• Former House Speaker Paul Renner stated that the law is necessary to protect children from addictive technologies.
• The ACLU of Florida's legislative director, Kara Gross, criticized HB 3 as a government censorship law that restricts access to information.
• The CCIA and co-plaintiff NetChoice filed a lawsuit in October 2024, arguing that HB 3 is an unconstitutional restriction on free speech.
• The CCIA is seeking a preliminary injunction to prevent the law from being implemented.
• Stephanie Joyce of CCIA described HB 3 as an 'internet rationing' law that blocks access to lawful content.
• The CCIA is an international trade association representing communications and technology companies, with a history of over 50 years.
